title: InferSlice: A Reference Architecture for SLO-driven LLM Inference over a Telco Wide-Area Network
summary: LLM inference is increasingly deployed as a core service for enterprise and interactive applications, but sovereignty, compliance, latency and resource-locality requirements can limit the suitability of centralised cloud deployments. Telco operators offer geographically distributed compute and network infrastructure for addressing these constraints. However, existing LLM serving frameworks are designed for tightly coupled data centres and provide limited support for coordinating geographically distributed and heterogeneous resources. We present InferSlice, a reference architecture for Service-Level Objective (SLO)-driven LLM inference over a telco infrastructure, integrating network slicing, GPU partitioning, elastic serving and observability. Led by BT in collaboration with the University of Bristol and NVIDIA, and realised on the JOINER UK national-scale wide-area network (WAN), InferSlice is evaluated on service differentiation across tiers, elastic scale-out, client-edge bandwidth as a bottleneck, and the reach of tensor, pipeline, data parallelism, and prefill/decode disaggregation over the WAN. Our results show that, on a general-purpose telco network, tiers yield distinct latency-throughput regimes, and weight streaming shortens scale-out time. Replication is placement-insensitive but memory-bound; pipeline parallelism tolerates near- and mid-cross-site hops, while tensor parallelism and disaggregation fail beyond a single subnet hop. We share practical insights from operating SLO-driven inference on a telco network, lessons learned and open questions, and hope to encourage further research on distributed and heterogeneous LLM inference systems.

title: Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond
summary: On-policy distillation aligns teacher feedback with a student's current behavior, yet acquiring useful supervision for multi-turn agents requires identifying both where guidance is needed and whether the student can sustain the interaction afterward. We introduce Frontier-OPD, which addresses this problem through the student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but admit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. To operationalize this frontier, Frontier-OPD organizes on-policy experience into a shared-state trajectory graph, where trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement identifies distinct intervention candidates while preserving the histories needed for replay. Short teacher bridges are then assessed by comparing agreement over the bridge and the ensuing student continuation with an equally long segment of the original trajectory, providing a behavioral proxy for guidance that the current student can build on. Accepted teacher responses augment ordinary distillation data, and fresh rollouts renew the frontier estimate as the policy changes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld report higher mean autonomous performance than the compared distillation baselines across the evaluated student scales and teacher configurations, with ablations indicating complementary effects of candidate selection and guidance filtering. In one ALFWorld timing setting, the additional collection cost is offset by a shorter time to a target success rate.

title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings. We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. Limiting the maximum number of output tokens has the largest impact, reducing energy use by up to 69% compared to the default configuration. On the execution side, 42 of 44 configurations produce code that consumes more energy per problem than the canonical human reference, with overheads ranging from +4% to +886%. The two exceptions achieve only marginal gains, with break-even points on the order of 10^6 to 10^7 executions. Mixture-of-Experts architectures consume substantially less inference energy than equivalently-sized dense models without sacrificing correctness, making architectural choice a more consequential sustainability lever than decoding parameters. Performance optimization and energy efficiency are not always aligned goals: LLM self-refinement consistently produces faster-seeking but energy-heavier code relative to what a human engineer would write. All artifacts are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170.

title: claude-code v2.1.309
summary:
What's changed

  • Fixed sandboxed Bash commands on macOS and Linux running the shell's startup files outside the sandbox before each command
  • Fixed macOS sandbox denyWrite glob patterns not applying at a path's real location when the pattern's folder is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits being able to modify the MCP config file passed with --mcp-config
  • Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions
  • Fixed the Bash permission check trusting a variable set by a command whose redirect can fail to open
  • Fixed Bash permission checks not prompting for some compound commands that change directory before running git when the cd is wrapped or prefixed, as they do for a plain cd
  • Fixed an Edit(path) deny rule not blocking a Bash redirect to that path in some commands that also held a subshell
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some locale-prefixed commands the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions on zsh accepting some arithmetic commands that the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktrees and branch checkouts that Claude Code creates so they ignore git replace refs, as its other git operations already do
  • Fixed profile store write protection not applying when the config directory is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sessions compacting repeatedly after reading files under a very large nested CLAUDE.md; a nested CLAUDE.md over the size limit now loads only its start
  • Fixed ctrl+enter (send now) only queuing a message when pressed before the response had started, and restarting a prompt's hooks while leaving the message queued when pressed while those hooks were running
  • Fixed key-bound slash commands running in the shell from ! mode
  • Fixed ctrl+o not showing messages from other agents and sessions that are still waiting to be delivered; they now appear in full under the transcript, marked as waiting
  • Fixed long tool output previews being cut through an emoji, leaving session transcripts that jq could not parse
  • Fixed Read reporting "File does not exist" for PDF page ranges in Linux sandboxes that share the parent's /proc
  • Fixed messages from a Claude Desktop-hosted session sometimes being lost when its connection refreshed
  • Fixed features missing from Claude Code sessions in the Claude desktop app when the terminal on the same computer was signed in to a different account or organization
  • Fixed the claude remote-control status line showing HEAD as the branch for a folder that is not in a git repository
  • Fixed split-pane agent teammates not inheriting the tool deny and --tools rules given on the leader's command line
  • Fixed sessions renamed with /rename appearing to other sessions under a generated name after a VS Code window reload or a non-interactive --resume
  • Fixed the /rewind list showing "No code changes" for a turn that changed checkpointed files through /code-review --fix, a subagent or a shell command
  • Fixed /privacy-settings showing an out-of-date "Help improve our AI models" value; it now also says when the setting can't be fetched
  • Fixed feedback saying "try again later" when your organization does not accept feedback; it now shows the server's reason and where to report a bug
  • Fixed oversized /feedback reports failing instead of being resent without the transcript
  • Fixed a skill in an --add-dir folder being unreachable when another skill already held its name; it is now offered as <folder>:<name>
  • Fixed /verify and /code-review not finding a nested package's own skill when its files were changed from the shell
  • Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that ant beta:worker poll --on-work passes trace context to the command
  • Fixed the /claude-api skill's C# tracing setup missing spans from the cloud platform clients
  • Fixed the /claude-api skill saying that API spans for requests to Claude Platform on AWS can't join the caller's trace
  • Fixed hooks that run in PowerShell not blocking when the hook's program exits with code 2, and on Windows PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks with "shell": "powershell" failing open when Git for Windows isn't installed
  • Fixed a mod's turn.step hook that names a model by alias, such as haiku, failing every request with a model error: the alias now resolves to its model
  • Fixed plugins and skills synced from claude.ai being removed, sometimes mid-session, after a disk read error
  • Fixed artifact publishes and updates being refused for some ordinary pages, such as pages with certain minified scripts or artifacts Claude could not read first
  • Fixed Claude asking for permission on each artifact update for the rest of a turn after the conversation was compacted in that turn
  • Fixed fine-grained tool streaming staying off on Amazon Bedrock when ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL is set to the default bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com endpoint
  • Fixed the "Waiting for API response" hint flickering behind gateways that send only keepalive pings: routes off Anthropic's backend now wait 45 seconds
  • Fixed Claude notifying unrelated GitHub users by writing role names and placeholders as mentions in PRs, issues and comments
  • Linux: Fixed sandbox write denies lifting when a background command outlived the session
  • Windows: Fixed PowerShell permission checks auto-approving some Set-Location or cd commands that target the current directory and carry extra arguments; these now prompt for approval
  • macOS: Fixed the "Install Command Line Developer Tools" dialog opening each time Claude Code starts on a Mac without Xcode or the Command Line Tools
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed --startup-timeout-min stopping a session whose first prompt, such as /code-review, was still working in a subagent; a frozen process is still stopped
  • Improved the speed of many git commands Claude Code runs for itself on Windows; on every platform, errors from those commands now show in English even when git is set to another language
  • Improved the error when a hooks module is nested too deep to load: it now names the file instead of showing a bare stack-overflow message
  • Improved disk-full handling: a Bash command cut off by a full disk now says so and names the folder to free up, and starting on a full temp volume prints a clear message, not a raw ENOSPC error
  • Improved the /claude-api skill to offer API tracing alongside SDK tracing when asked to add OpenTelemetry
  • Improved the /claude-api skill to check the live docs before saying a feature is unsupported
  • Self-hosted runner: Improved sessions that move to a new runner: Claude now sees the tool call that was interrupted, marked as outcome unknown
  • Updated the bundled dataviz skill to accept APCA as a text-contrast measure (keeping WCAG 2 ratios where AA conformance is required), add an apca(text, background) function to its palette validator scripts, and say whether a label inside a colored chart fill should be white or near-black
  • Updated the /claude-api skill: service account keys and Workload Identity Federation tokens can now manage OpenTelemetry destinations
  • Changed sed -i to get the standard Bash prompt and run as written, not a simulated file-edit preview; like other Bash edits, it is no longer restored by /rewind
  • Changed claude ultrareview to require workspace trust: it asks on a terminal, else refuses; scripts pass --trust-workspace, which takes no value (put a PR number or base branch before it), or set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRAREVIEW_TRUST_CHECK=1
  • Changed the dangerous rm and rmdir prompt in bypass permissions mode in the Desktop app and VS Code to deny the command at once with a rewrite hint, so unattended sessions keep going
  • Changed commands the settings exclude from the sandbox to ask before writing to its write-list paths while the sandbox is enabled but cannot run; the unsandboxed fallback is refused there
  • Changed worktree creation and reuse so git no longer fetches objects on demand, in ordinary clones and in partial clones with a Bash sandbox configured; such a partial clone fetches them first
  • Changed the /claude-api skill to build Managed Agents subagent teams on multiagent_20261001 with dynamic workflows on by default, instead of coordinator
  • [VSCode] Added a log warning that says what to do when dictation or the extension's own requests fail certificate verification, such as behind a TLS-inspecting proxy
  • [VSCode] Fixed the Claude panel staying blank after the editor cached an incomplete copy of its files; it now recovers by itself, or says what went wrong and how to fix it
  • [VSCode] Fixed Session history filling up with empty "Untitled" sessions each time you start a new session without sending a message
  • [VSCode] Fixed long slash-command messages such as /goal filling the chat panel; they now fold behind Show more like other prompts (#97469)
  • [VSCode] Fixed long messages not folding behind Show more after the chat panel is made narrower
  • [VSCode] Fixed Ctrl+J in the chat input always inserting a newline: it is now left to VS Code and the OS when "ctrl+j" is set to null in the Chat context of ~/.claude/keybindings.json
  • [VSCode] Fixed a mod's "From the … plugin" label above the prompt being drawn over the slash command and @-mention menus (#102981)
  • [VSCode] Fixed an empty list item, paragraph or code block, and list items renumbered from 1, when pasting copied LaTeX math
  • [VSCode] Fixed the feedback error showing only an HTTP status when your organization does not accept feedback
  • [VSCode] Improved Edit and Write speed in the chat panel: the wait for new problems after each edit is now 0.75 seconds in most cases, down from 1 to 1.5 seconds
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the Add connector list in routine forms saying no connectors were available while they were still loading
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the cloud environment editor shuffling environment variables and adding backslashes to values that contain both kinds of quote
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the self-hosted environment details dialog in admin settings so its title, tabs and buttons stay in view while only the content scrolls
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed the "read documentation" tool row in cloud sessions, which showed escaped JSON instead of a readable page
  • [Cloud sessions] Improved a cloud session's Changes pane, which now says when it lists only pushed commits or only Claude's edits
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in Slack posting a draft you approved for a channel into your DM by mistake; a post with no channel is now refused so it can go to the approved channel
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Allow and Deny on Claude's approval cards in Slack doing nothing when the session had stopped; your answer now restarts the session
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude ignoring untagged messages in a Slack channel after its workspace moved to a different Claude organization, including unshared channels on Enterprise Grid
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude in a Slack channel posting a threaded reply before reading a newer message someone had just added to that thread
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed the Slack page in Claude Tag admin settings saying no workspaces were connected when the list failed to load; it now shows an error with a Retry button
  • [Code Review] Fixed a finished review showing no check on the pull request when earlier tries to create it failed; a final try now adds a completed check
  • [Code Review] Fixed a push queued behind a running review still starting a review after @claude review stop; its check now closes and says why

title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
summary: Evaluating conversational agents that act on live, mutable enterprise data is hard: replayed sessions drift as backend state changes, and a benchmark built today can silently go stale as the data it describes moves on. We present an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that stays reproducible despite the live data it operates on changing, and that can be regenerated on demand once it goes stale. We then use this harness as the fitness function for GEPA-based prompt optimization under a correctness gate that guards against reward hacking. Applied to a production merchant-facing agent, correctness-gated compression shrinks the agent's full prompt surface by 3.5-7.6% without regressing held-out task correctness, consistently across three independent subject-model families, and for one, correctness measurably improves.

title: Cycle-of-Thought: Self-Evaluative Iterative Reasoning for Table Visual Question Answering in Document Images
summary: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have significantly improved Visual Question Answering (VQA) performance, yet their reasoning over structured content such as tables remains inconsistent, often plagued by spatial misalignment and logical hallucinations. Existing approaches for improving table VQA typically rely on architectural modifications or expensive supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which impose high barriers to entry due to the need for large-scale, expert-annotated datasets and significant computational resources. In this work, we propose Self-RefineVQA, a training-free, inference-time self-correction framework that improves table VQA performance without additional labeled data or model updates. Inspired by human revision behavior, our method enables a single VLM to iteratively act as a generator, critic, and refiner, forming a closed self-feedback loop that corrects common reasoning errors through prompt-guided re-evaluation. Experiments on tabular VQA benchmarks demonstrate that Self-RefineVQA yields consistent accuracy gains in monolingual and cross-lingual understanding, with a particularly significant boost for small models, enabling lightweight models (e.g., 2B-7B parameters) to rival the performance of significantly larger counterparts. Furthermore, we provide a comparative complexity analysis demonstrating that while inference cost increases linearly, our framework offers superior data efficiency and a lower cumulative cost by eliminating the prohibitive annotation bottleneck of human labeling required for fine-tuning. Our results highlight the potential of prompt-based self-improvement as a scalable, accessible paradigm for reliable table reasoning in VLMs.

title: vllm v0.32.0
summary:
v0.32.0

Highlights

This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)!

  • Structured decisions and generic parsers: the new POST /v1/systemone endpoint answers choice, noul and score questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on Cloudflare/clef-omni (#61064), LiquidAI/d1-3B (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new hf tool and reasoning parser (--tool-call-parser hf, --reasoning-parser hf) reads the checkpoint's response_template, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005).
  • Low-precision KV cache everywhere: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); fp8_ds_mla on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit ultraquant_4bit KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057).
  • Model Runner V2: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360).
  • Faster startup and serving: vllm download-kernels installs FlashInfer's precompiled kernels (#58765); vllm preload --preload-autotune keeps the FlashInfer autotune table warm across restarts (#60085); a shared-memory tensor arena broadcasts large multimodal tensors to workers with one copy (#51207); tokenizers and processors load from the local snapshot (#60825); and with --api-server-count above 1 each connection goes to the least-loaded API worker, for 43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in the PR's benchmark (#60723).
  • Model support: new EmbeddingGemma 2 omni-modal embeddings (#60254), MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674) and Nemotron 3.5 ASR (#59827); video input in the Transformers modeling backend (#57441); GLM-5.3 sparse MLA index conversions reused across layers (3.5-3.9x on that kernel, #59464) and fused multi-step draft decode (13.3% at concurrency 1, #57443); HiSparse per-request residency caching for up to 58% more throughput on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200 with long, fully GPU-resident contexts at high concurrency (#60083).
  • Security: fixes for GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7 (chat template resource exhaustion, #50300), GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4 (tokenizer max_token_id, #59491) and GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9 (P2P ZMQ socket exhaustion, #51504); CORS no longer allows every origin by default (#61009); untrusted images are limited to raster formats (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are signed (#59357); and JSON schemas nested deeper than 64 levels are rejected (#60036).
  • Breaking changes: Python 3.10 dropped (#60402); default CORS origins restricted (#61009); transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 and tokenizers>=0.23.2 (#57387, #59796); torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes removed (#60517); cascade attention removed (#61126); mamba_cache_mode="all" removed (#58997); max_tokens no longer reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API reasoning stream events renamed (#59652).

Model Support

Security

  • GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7: chat templates are validated statically and rendered under a timeout (VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT), user-supplied chat_template in Responses chat_template_kwargs is rejected, and the Rust frontend caps template execution (#50300).
  • GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4: tokenizer max_token_id off-by-one fixed (#59491).
  • GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9: P2P ZMQ peer sessions are bounded by VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS (default 128), VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30) and VLLM_P2P_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S (default 300), so unique peer addresses can no longer exhaust ZMQ sockets (#51504).
  • Default CORS settings no longer allow every origin in the Python and Rust frontends; set --allowed-origins to permit browser origins (#61009).
  • Untrusted images are opened with a raster-format allowlist (ALLOWED_IMAGE_FORMATS), denying EPS/PostScript and WMF (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are HMAC-signed and forged handles rejected (#59357).
  • Structured-output JSON schemas nested more than 64 levels return 400 (#60036); chunked /v1/embeddings requests keep cache_salt (#47696); Phi-4 MM audio no longer holds multi-GiB attention matrices (#60614); DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum pixel tensors no longer kill EngineCore (#59417).
  • Security dependency bumps: aiohttp>=3.14.3, pillow>=12.3.0, cryptography, urllib3, pyjwt and others (#59249, #59315, #59427).

  • transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 (minimum raised from 5.10.4, #57387, #59762) and tokenizers>=0.23.2 (#59796).
  • NIXL 1.5.0 (#56907), CuTe DSL 4.8.0 block-scale APIs (#59480), humming-kernels==0.1.17 with initial Rubin support (#61556, #61858), InstantTensor 0.2.2 (#61167), and flashinfer-jit-cache excluded from wheel install_requires (#60052).
  • ROCm: AITER 0.1.24.post1 (#59794) and MoRI v1.2.3.post1 (#56073). XPU: auto-round-lib 0.16.0 (#60976). TPU: tpu-inference v0.31.0 (#60190).

Build

  • Python 3.11-3.14 supported (#60402); macOS wheels built with the stable ABI (#60312); CUDA source builds require GCC 13 and fail early otherwise (#60259); Docker images compile Python bytecode at build time for faster container startup (#55422); VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED finds a compatible published wheel within the last 20 commits (#58871); the vendored DeepGEMM uses TORCH_LIBRARY (abi3, #48962).

Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Python 3.10 is no longer supported; the minimum is Python 3.11 (#60402).
  • Default CORS origins changed from * to none; set --allowed-origins for browser clients (#61009).
  • transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 and tokenizers>=0.23.2 are required (#57387, #59796).
  • The torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes were removed, along with PassConfig.enable_sp, fuse_gemm_comms and sp_min_token_num; model-level sequence parallelism is unaffected (#60517).
  • Cascade attention was removed; --disable-cascade-attn still parses but only warns and will be removed in v0.33.0 (#61126).
  • mamba_cache_mode="all" was removed; --mamba-cache-mode all now fails validation (#58997).
  • Previously deprecated APIs were removed: wait_for_inflight_requests (use mode="wait"), AsyncLLM.pause_generation(), IOProcessor.output_to_response, vllm.scripts.main() and vllm bench throughput --dataset (#60923). The sonnet benchmark dataset was removed as scheduled (#60129). Tensorizer support was removed from LoRA (#60024), and the PyO3 vllm._rust_tool_parser bridge was removed (#59744).
  • API changes: max_tokens is treated as an upper bound on output rather than reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API streaming uses response.content_part.added/done with part.type="reasoning_text" instead of response.reasoning_part.added/done (#59652); SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids is per row (#56984); /inference/v1/generate logprobs use integer token IDs (#58181); sleep API responses are standardized and invalid levels return 400 (#52864); return_mm_kwargs is deprecated in favor of mm_payload (#61427).
  • Watermarking: when the engine has watermarking configured, an omitted request field means enabled and only false opts out; unsupported combinations warn and fall back (#56801).
  • Rust frontend: qwen3_xml now parses Qwen3-Coder XML (alias of qwen3_coder); use the new qwen3_json for the JSON format (#60136).
  • New defaults: shared-memory tensor arena on (#51207); GLM-5.x FP8 KV cache on SM100 with --kv-cache-dtype auto (#60140, #60281); VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_HYBRID_MODE=1 (#57991); Humming preferred over Marlin on SM90 (#56997); sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor 2 above 256K max_model_len (#61023); MRV2 on ROCm with model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360); VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=auto (#59965); dtype=auto picks bfloat16 on PowerPC (#58528); MXFP4 W4A4 checkpoints fall back to W4A16 with a warning when no W4A4 kernel exists (#60079).
  • Stricter validation: incompatible --prefix-match-unit (#58021), max_num_scheduled_tokens=0 (#60714), HiSparse with cudagraph_mode=FULL (#59688), and negative --device-ids (#49053) are rejected at startup.
